result.title: Recursive Self-Editing: LLMs Program Their Own Weight Edits for Self-Improvement
result.summary: Recursive self-improvement asks a system to improve the very system that improves it. Today's language models improve themselves through data, training recipes or scaffolds. Whenever their weights change, gradient descent writes the update, not the model. We let the model write its own weights. In SELFWRITE, each generation the current model studies its own reasoning on fresh training problems, inspects its own weights and activations in a persistent Python session, and writes a program that constructs a low-rank weight edit for itself from white-box primitives (singular directions, activation contrasts between its right and wrong answers, rank-one projections, tensor computations), with no training or gradient tool. Every candidate is graded once on a hidden gate set against the current model; the best strictly improving edit is merged into the weights, and the edited model writes the next edit. On Qwen3.8-27B and math problems from DAPO-Math, five generations of SELFWRITE raise gate accuracy from 73.95% to 76.45% and accuracy on a held-out test split that the loop never sees from 76.30% to 77.75% (avg@4) and from 82.60% to 84.80% (pass@4), without a single gradient step. A language model can author useful changes to its own weights without gradients, and the edited model keeps writing useful edits.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 SELFWRITE：让语言模型在持久 Python 会话中查看自身权重与激活，自行编写程序构造低秩权重编辑，并用隐藏门控集选出严格提升的编辑合并进权重，换代循环，全程不使用梯度；在数学题上经过五代迭代带来小幅准确率提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 非多模态工作，但「用正确/错误答案的激活对比构造秩一投影与低秩编辑」以及按门控集筛选编辑的做法，可供核查如何在不依赖梯度训练时塑造或筛选内部推理状态、并为正确与错误轨迹分配贡献。
